thread.title: Singapore Shares Tipped To End Losing Streak

author: rttnews.com
title: Singapore Shares Tipped To End Losing Streak
text:
The Singapore stock market has moved lower in three consecutive trading days, sliding almost 30 points or 0.9 percent along the way. The Straits Times Index now rests just beneath the 3,175-point plateau although it may find traction on Thursday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly positive on an improved outlook for interest rates and a spike in crude oil prices. The European and U.S. markets were up and the Asian bourses are predicted to follow suit.
The STI finished modestly lower on Wednesday following losses from the financials and plantations, while the industrials were mixed.
For the day, the index fell 13.31 points or 0.42 percent to end at 3,174.38 after trading between 3,169.29 and 3,194.28. Volume was 1.4 billion shares worth 1.17 billion Singapore dollars. There were 215 gainers and 166 decliners.
Among the actives, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding surged 3.65 percent, while Hutchison Port Holdings soared 2.00 percent, Golden Agri-Resources plummeted 1.92 percent, CapitaLand Mall Trust plunged 1.67 percent, Ascendas REIT tumbled 1.45 percent, Thai Beverage skidded 1.35 percent, DBS Group dropped 1.16 percent, SembCorp Industries retreated 1.15 percent, United Overseas Bank declined 0.90 percent, Comfort DelGro jumped 0.44 percent, Singapore Exchange climbed 0.39 percent, SingTel and Keppel Corp both shed 0.33 percent, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation eased 0.09 percent and CapitaLand, Genting Singapore and Wilmar International were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is firm in response to the Federal Reserve's monetary policy announcement, which sent the major averages to nearly two-month closing highs.
The Dow added 434.90 points or 1.77 while the NASDAQ surged 154.79 points or 2.20 rose 41.05 points or 1.55 percent to 2,681.05.
Stocks accelerated to the upside after the Fed
Positive sentiment was also generated by solid earnings news from companies like Boeing (BA) and Apple (AAPL).
 West Texas Intermediate Crude oil futures barrel.
